newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas recovers on cold Midwest weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas recovers on cold Midwest weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices recovered from last week's lows Monday as colder weather in the Midwest and southern plains rekindled some buying interest, sources said.
Swing prices on the Gulf Coast pipes rose by about 40 cents to the mid-to-high $2.90s per mmBtu, as arctic air seeped into northern Texas.
Temperatures in Dallas Tuesday are forecast to dip to highs in the 30s F.
In south Texas, prices gained about 35 cents to the $2.80-2.85 range.
In the Midcontinent, prices jumped into the $2.90-2.95 range, up about 45 cents from Friday's levels.
The storage deficit to year-ago levels in the Producing Region left most buyers relying on the spot market to meet the rising heating demand.
According to American Gas Association, storage inventories as of Jan 10 in the Producing Region were at 440 bcf, or 49 percent full. This is compared with 484 bcf a year ago.
In west Texas, Permian prices were up about 40 cents in the low-$2.80s to about $2.90 as colder air approached.
Houston Lighting and Power's 1,250 megawatt South Texas 1 nuclear power unit restarted after shutting down briefly this past weekend.
Prices at the southern California border gained about 35 cents to about $2.90.
In the East, prices hovered around $3.40 at the New York city-gate, which was about even with Friday's highs.
